questions.q: What is identity, according to Taylor?
questions.a: A person's understanding of who they are
w: A person's position in society
The way a person dresses
The laws and traditions of a country

questions.q: How is a person's identity partly shaped?
questions.a: By recognition and the opinions of others
w: Only by their own decisions
Only by their family background
By their economic situation

questions.a: Seeing a person or group through a false or negative image
w: Treating everyone in exactly the same way
Giving people too many opportunities
Refusing to agree with someone's opinions

questions.a: It can cause people to develop a negative image of themselves.
w: It can make people lose interest in politics.
It can cause people to question every social rule.
It can prevent people from learning about other cultures.

questions.q: What does it mean to internalize a negative image?
questions.a: To begin believing negative ideas about yourself
w: To understand why other people have different opinions
To refuse to listen to criticism
To change your identity to fit into a new society

questions.q: Taylor discusses the experiences of women. What problem does he identify?
questions.a: Some women began to believe that they were inferior to men.
w: Women were given too many opportunities.
Women were encouraged to become political leaders.
Women were unable to understand their own identities.

questions.q: According to Taylor, why might people struggle to use new opportunities even after social barriers are removed?
questions.a: They may have internalized negative beliefs about themselves.
w: They may not have enough education.
They may prefer traditional social hierarchies.
They may not want to compete with other people.

questions.q: What example does Taylor give concerning Black people in white society?
questions.a: Society projected negative images of them, which some began to believe.
w: They were encouraged to reject their cultural identities.
They were given more opportunities than other groups.
They were expected to adopt European traditions.

questions.q: What does Taylor say about the treatment of Indigenous and colonized people?
questions.a: Europeans often described them as inferior and uncivilized.
w: They were generally recognized as equal by European societies.
They were encouraged to preserve their identities.
They were responsible for creating negative stereotypes about Europeans.

questions.q: According to Taylor, is recognition simply a matter of good manners?
questions.a: No. It is a vital human need.
w: Yes. It means being polite to everyone.
Yes. It means avoiding disagreements with others.
No. It is only important for minority groups.
